concepts.name: Big-O notation
concepts.gloss: Asymptotic upper bounds on running time.

concepts.name: Polynomials
concepts.gloss: Sums of coefficients times powers of a variable, with addition and multiplication.

concepts.name: Complex numbers
concepts.gloss: Numbers a+bi with i²=−1, with modulus and unit-modulus phases.

concepts.name: Multitape Turing machine
concepts.gloss: A Turing machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes, each head moving at most one cell per step.

concepts.name: The n log n barrier
concepts.gloss: The Schönhage–Strassen conjecture that n log n is the optimal multiplication cost on multitape Turing machines, and the Harvey–van der Hoeven O(n log n) multiplier, which is used here only as a subroutine on short inputs.

evidence.quote: proposed $n\log n$ as the optimal order of growth
Scanning an array of $\Theta(n)$ stored bits at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$.
Calls to the established $O(n\log n)$ multiplier are ordinary subroutine calls

concepts.name: Convolution
concepts.gloss: The cyclic convolution of two coefficient lists, equal to the product of the corresponding polynomials modulo x^S − 1.

evidence.quote: Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to convolution of short integer coefficients.

concepts.name: Radix-digit convolution
concepts.gloss: Writing each n-bit integer as a polynomial in 2^b with b-bit digits, so the integer product is the digit convolution followed by carry propagation.

evidence.quote: Write the two inputs as polynomials in $2^b$, each with $q=\lceil n/b\rceil$ nonnegative digits.
Propagate radix-$2^b$ carries in increasing coefficient order.

concepts.name: Discrete Fourier transform
concepts.gloss: The normalized transform F_q that averages inputs weighted by roots of unity; it turns convolution into pointwise multiplication.

evidence.quote: (F_q u)_k=\frac1q\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}u_j e^{-2\pi i jk/q}
The normalized convolution rule is

concepts.name: Fast Fourier transform with butterflies
concepts.gloss: Computing a length-2^a transform in a levels, each pairing entries by a two-point butterfly H₀(u,v)=((u+v)/2,(u−v)/2) followed by a twiddle multiplication.

evidence.quote: the decimation-in-frequency step pairs $z_k$ with $z_{k+t/2}$ for $0\leq k<t/2$
the transform calculation consists of address rearrangements, signed shifts, and two-point butterfly operations

concepts.name: Fixed-point complex grid and truncation
concepts.gloss: Complex numbers stored as signed two's-complement numerators over 2^p, in the unit disk, with truncation toward zero to the grid after exact dyadic arithmetic.

evidence.quote: Let $Q_p$ truncate the real and imaginary parts of every coefficient toward zero to $2^{-p}\mathbb Z$.
\mathbb D_p=\{2^{-p}(a+ib):a,b\in\mathbb Z,\ a^2+b^2\leq 2^{2p}\}

concepts.name: Contractions and error accounting
concepts.gloss: Linear maps that do not increase the maximum-modulus norm; composing approximations adds their errors, which is how the accumulated numerical error is bounded.

evidence.quote: Composing such algorithms adds their errors: at each step, insert the exact map at the computed input and use its contraction bound on the accumulated input error.
Each normalized Fourier transform above is a contraction

concepts.name: Subspaces, rank and orthogonal complements
concepts.gloss: Matrix rank, subspaces with a bilinear form, nondegenerate subspaces, orthogonal complements and orthonormal bases, as used to label a network.

evidence.quote: A label is a nondegenerate subspace of a fixed bilinear space.
its dimension is the absolute change in label dimension

concepts.name: Arrays as address fields on tape
concepts.gloss: An array indexed by a product of ranges is stored in lexicographic order; its logical volume V is the number of data bits, and elementary field moves, digit permutations and row splits cost O(V).

evidence.quote: An array with address set $[a_1]\times\cdots\times[a_t]$ is stored in lexicographic order, with the first coordinate most significant.
The \emph{logical volume} $V$ is the number of stored data bits.
Each of the following operations on an array of volume $V$ takes $O(V)$ steps on a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes

concepts.name: Controlled cyclic shift
concepts.gloss: Adding to a target address field an offset computed from earlier control fields, modulo a range, in O(V) time by splitting and re-merging blocks.

evidence.quote: Suppose a target field $y\in[Q]$ follows its control fields, each control used in an offset having $O(b)$ digits.

concepts.name: Scratch-restoring bank exchange
concepts.gloss: A fixed linear network of copy, gather, scatter and side-injection gates that swaps two banks of values in three stages while returning every auxiliary (scratch) wire to its arbitrary initial value.

evidence.quote: We construct two fixed linear networks that exchange two banks of values while restoring every auxiliary value.
the last two restore the scratch values

concepts.name: Frames: changing representation along a network
concepts.gloss: Replacing each scalar wire by an array and storing it as D_v g for an invertible operator D_v (a frame), so that a pointwise linear gate commutes with the frame and only the endpoint operator remains.

evidence.quote: We call $D_v$ its frame: the stored array is $D_vg$ when the logical array is $g$.
At a pointwise linear gate $G$, the common frame commutes with the gate:

concepts.name: Triple-subset labels and the rank budget
concepts.gloss: Subspaces of a fixed space attached to gates and terminals, built from indicator vectors of three-element subsets so that adjacent labels are nested and the total edge rank s is strictly less than the wire count W times the dimension m.

evidence.quote: The construction uses three-element subsets: gather and scatter create coefficients depending on intersection size, and auxiliary wires cancel the unwanted coefficients.
The decisive property is that the total number $s$ of smaller calls satisfies $s<Wm$.

concepts.name: Address shear and triangular factorization
concepts.gloss: The address map (H,D)↦(H+AD,D) for a rational matrix A of rank a, performed with exactly a interchanges of smaller field pairs after factoring A=E₁ΠE₂ into lower-triangular factors and a partial permutation.

evidence.quote: Every rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$ has a factorization
can be performed with exactly $a$ interchanges of pairs of $b$-digit fields and $O(V)$ further work

concepts.name: Recursive rank saving
concepts.gloss: Splitting rows among the W network roles makes each recursive call a 1/W-volume stream, so the cost per volume grows by s/W<m when the parameter is multiplied by m, giving a power saving.

evidence.quote: After dividing cost by volume, multiplying the parameter by $m$ increases the recursive contribution by $s/W<m$. This strict inequality is the source of the power saving.

concepts.name: Power-width chunk interchange
concepts.gloss: Interchanging two chunks of e=m^k digits in time O(V e^τ) by running the bit network on W role streams, with each edge shear implemented recursively by smaller interchanges.

evidence.quote: The chunks can be interchanged in $O(Ve^\tau)$ time, preserving every other address field, on a fixed number of finite-alphabet tapes.

concepts.name: Address chunk interchange
concepts.gloss: Interchanging two disjoint contiguous address fields of u bits of an array in O(V u^τ) time for a fixed τ<1, using XOR combinations of intermediate data although the final effect is an exact permutation.

evidence.quote: Its cost is $O(Vu^\tau)$ for a fixed $\tau<1$.
Although its final effect is an exact permutation, its intermediate steps form pointwise XOR combinations of data.

concepts.name: Complex phase network
concepts.gloss: The second network over Gaussian dyadics with binary labels, whose frames are built from the two-point kernel C=HSH=aI+bX, so each edge is a product of translation kernels and the endpoint operator is C^{⊗m} on every role.

evidence.quote: For the numerical procedure, the endpoint operator becomes the simultaneous $H_0$ layer after diagonal phase operations and a dyadic scale.
Each procedure arises from its own fixed linear network that exchanges two banks of values, with prescribed signs, and restores every auxiliary value.

concepts.name: Packed selected-bit addition
concepts.gloss: XORing corresponding selected bits of many chunks at once by a constant number of whole-chunk cyclic shifts that are correct away from a small set of guard-violating addresses, which are then repaired deterministically by sorting.

evidence.quote: of cyclic shifts of whole chunk ranges, then corrects an explicitly bounded set of addresses

concepts.name: Simultaneous butterfly layer
concepts.gloss: Applying H₀ to the same bit position in each of D≤d address chunks at once, on polynomial records of complex fixed-point coefficients, in O(V d^{λ'}) time with one final truncation.

evidence.quote: and the cost is $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ for a fixed $\lambda'<1$
whereas separate butterfly factors would require $D$ whole-array passes.

concepts.name: Polynomial ring modulo y^r + 1
concepts.gloss: Complex polynomials of degree less than r with y^r=−1, in which powers of y are roots of unity and multiplication by y^a is a signed shift of the coefficient list.

evidence.quote: one coordinate is stored as the coefficient list of a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$, with $r$ a power of two
Multiplication by $y^a$, for any integer $a$, permutes the coefficients and changes some signs

concepts.title: Polynomial ring modulo $y^r + 1$

symbols.name: ring variable
symbols.meaning: The formal polynomial variable whose powers act as roots of unity because y^r=−1.

symbols.name: record length
symbols.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in a polynomial record, a power of two.

concepts.name: Synthetic polynomial transform
concepts.gloss: A Fourier-type transform over the negacyclic ring whose roots of unity ω_t=y^{2r/t} are signed coefficient shifts, so each twiddle multiplication is free of real arithmetic.

evidence.quote: For a power of two $t$ dividing $2r$, define $\omega_t=y^{2r/t}$.
multiplication by such a root is a signed shift of the coefficient list

concepts.name: Retained frequency order
concepts.gloss: The forward transform writes outputs in bit-reversed order; the pointwise product and the opposite transform both use this order, so no permutation is ever executed.

evidence.quote: The two forward synthetic transforms retain the same frequency order through their pointwise product, and the opposite transform consumes that order.

concepts.name: Transform layout on tape
concepts.gloss: Placing the selected bit of each participating axis at a common offset in consecutive K-bit chunks, using bit moves and chunk interchanges, so that each transform round is one simultaneous butterfly layer.

evidence.quote: we must place the selected bits of the participating axes at a common offset in consecutive $K$-bit chunks

concepts.name: Signed packing (Kronecker substitution)
concepts.gloss: Multiplying two polynomials with small signed integer coefficients by evaluating them at a large power of two, multiplying the resulting integers with the O(n log n) multiplier, and extracting coefficients with centered carries.

evidence.quote: Signed coefficient packing is a form of Kronecker substitution

concepts.name: Normalized convolution over the polynomial ring
concepts.gloss: Convolving arrays of ring elements by two forward synthetic transforms, a pointwise polynomial product divided by r, and the opposite transform, giving (f*g)/T with a bounded error.

evidence.quote: Perform both forward transforms and retain their common $LB$ order.

concepts.name: Cyclic-to-negacyclic coefficient twist
concepts.gloss: Multiplying coefficient k by ζ^k with ζ=e^{πi/r} maps cyclic convolution on the last axis to convolution modulo y^r+1; untwisting recovers the cyclic result.

evidence.quote: A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$; its negative wrap gives precisely the original cyclic wrap after the twist is removed.
is well defined, since $(\zeta y)^r=(-1)(-1)=1$

concepts.name: Bluestein chirp identity
concepts.gloss: Rewriting a Fourier transform, including a frequency permutation, as pointwise chirp phases around a cyclic convolution with the chirp.

evidence.quote: Next, Bluestein's chirp identity converts the middle transform, including its target permutation, into normalized cyclic convolution.

concepts.name: Gaussian resampling
concepts.gloss: Harvey–van der Hoeven's way to compute a Fourier transform of prime length s from one of power-of-two length t>s using Gaussian-weighted linear maps A and B₀ that are contractions.

evidence.quote: Gaussian resampling then expresses each source Fourier transform through a power-of-two tensor transform.
it replaces the Fourier transforms needed for this convolution by multidimensional transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two

concepts.name: Retained permutation cancellation
concepts.gloss: The coordinate permutations of resampling are kept in the transform formula; the source permutation cancels between the two forward transforms, the pointwise product and the opposite-sign transform, so no full sorts are executed.

evidence.quote: Finally, the source permutation retained during resampling cancels across the two forward source transforms, their pointwise product, and the opposite-sign transform.
so they need not be executed as separate full sorts

concepts.name: Chinese-remainder address map
concepts.gloss: An algebra isomorphism sending the radix-digit coefficient list onto a product of pairwise coprime cyclic axes while preserving convolution, implemented by triangular controlled shifts and axis reorderings.

evidence.quote: Agarwal and Cooley used the Chinese remainder theorem to convert one cyclic convolution into multidimensional cyclic convolution
the radix-digit coefficient list is placed on a product of distinct prime cyclic axes by a Chinese-remainder map that preserves convolution

concepts.name: Source transform on the padded box
concepts.gloss: The approximate source Fourier transform formed by linewise Gaussian maps A, the chirp convolution of length T on the padded power-of-two box, linewise B₀ and an exact 2^γ scale, equal to R F_s on the prime-length source.

evidence.quote: The source arrays are stored in the padded power-of-two box, with zeros outside the valid source coordinates.

concepts.name: Parameter regime for the multiplier
concepts.gloss: The choice of precision p=6b, dimension d≈p^ε, record length r=2^Θ(p^(1−ε)), power-of-two axis lengths t_i and distinct prime source lengths s_i just below them, so that Tp=Θ(n) and all hypotheses hold.

evidence.quote: p=6b,\quad d=\lfloor b^\epsilon\rfloor
The distinct prime lengths $s_i$ must be close to the powers of two $t_i$

concepts.name: Precision and exact recovery
concepts.gloss: Disk-margin and error bounds showing the recovered convolution coefficients are within error below 1/2 of integers below 2^{3b}, so rounding and carry propagation give the exact product.

evidence.quote: proves that the recovered coefficient error is strictly below $1/2$, and propagates carries to obtain the exact binary product
The strict error below $1/2$ makes the nearest integer to that value the unique correct coefficient.

concepts.name: The multiplication algorithm
concepts.gloss: Digit conversion, the CRT map Φ, two forward source transforms, a pointwise product, one opposite transform, two scalings by S, rounding, inverse Φ and carry propagation to output the 2n-bit product.

evidence.quote: Apply the coefficient-address map $\Phi$, with its padded layout, to obtain source arrays $u,v$.
The two occurrences of $S$ in this algorithm undo different normalizations.

concepts.name: Cost accounting and the exponent κ
concepts.gloss: Dividing every cost by V=Tp gives normalized costs that are at most p^(1−2κ), the smallest margin 2^−181 coming from the chunk-exchange term, giving total time O(n(log n)^(1−κ)).

evidence.quote: Thus $\min_i g_i=2^{-181}=2\kappa$.
Each of the seven displayed powers is at most $1-2\kappa$

concepts.name: Integer multiplication below n log n
concepts.gloss: A deterministic multitape Turing machine multiplying two n-bit integers in O(n(lg n)^(1−κ)) time with κ=2^−182, disproving the n log n optimality conjecture in this model.

evidence.quote: We give a deterministic algorithm that multiplies two $n$-bit integers in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ worst-case time, with $\kappa=2^{-182}$
disproves the $n\log n$ optimality conjecture of Sch\"onhage and Strassen in this model
